newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: BOURSE RAISES A GROUP REQUIREMENTS.
newsitem.headline: BOURSE RAISES A GROUP REQUIREMENTS.

text.p: Lithuania's stock exchange said on Monday that its board decided to raise the standards for the stocks of the companies listed on its A group.
The group A of the Vilnius bourse lists the 45 most active stocks.

"The board of the bourse decided that the A group stocks must be traded no less than three times during the last month," Saulius Malinauskas, the head of the bourse's listing department, told Reuters.
Previously a company only had to be quoted three times in one year to remain on the list.
The bourse also decided to add a profit requrement to A group companies.
"In the previous year or for the first half of the current year the company must operate profitably," Malinauskas added.
He also said that a stock should be listed no less than one month on the current list of the bourse before it will be included on the A list.
Malinauskas said that the board of the bourse will have the right to delist A group shares if the company reports losses for the last year or for the first half of the current year.
The board of the bourse may also delist the company from the A group if the liquidity of the shares is not high enough though a concrete liquidity rate was not imposed, Malinauskas said.
The decision comes into force from August 18, he added.
